title: Mean of a diagonal section
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability distribution $\pi$, and suppose the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ have a finite nonempty orthonormal basis for the $\pi$-weighted inner product that contains the constant-one function. For any nonnegative integer $n$, coordinate $j$, and function $h$ assigning a function on $\Omega^n$ to each $\omega\in\Omega$, assume $h(\omega,x')=h(\omega,x)$ whenever $x'$ is obtained from $x$ by replacing coordinate $j$ with $\omega$. Then the product mean of $x\mapsto h(x_j,x)$ equals the $\pi$-mean, over $\omega$, of the product mean of $x\mapsto h(\omega,x)$.
hypotheses_covered: π is a probability distribution on Ω
